claims.text: Direct contact between W and CuCrZr exhibits a significant thermal-expansion mismatch.
The thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr produces high residual stresses.
Direct W–CuCrZr contact has compromised interfacial bonding.
A functionally graded nanolaminate interlayer can be deposited between W and CuCrZr using physical vapor deposition.
The interlayer composition would transition from a W-compatible end to a CuCrZr-compatible end.
The graded nanolaminate can be designed to have an effective coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
A gradual transition in thermal-expansion properties minimizes residual thermal stresses.
The graded interlayer forms robust metallurgical bonds at both the W-side and CuCrZr-side interfaces.
Reduced residual stress and robust bonding lower the risk of interlayer delamination.
Reduced residual stress and robust bonding lower the risk of interface cracking under extreme conditions.
The graded nanolaminate will improve interface integrity between W and CuCrZr.
Improved interface integrity will enhance the mechanical stability and durability of the W–CuCrZr joint under fusion-reactor operating conditions.
Directly bonded W and CuCrZr can fail prematurely under extreme thermal and irradiation conditions.
The benefit of the interlayer depends on precise control of its compositional gradient.
Improper compositional gradation could introduce interlayer cracking or delamination.
Excessively thick interlayers could introduce interlayer cracking or delamination.
Optimal compositional gradients and layer thicknesses have not been fully quantified.
Long-term stability of the proposed interlayer under continuous irradiation and thermal cycling has not been established.
